prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val2] SLA tiers (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Tier" · longest unbreakable word 75px · one-line width 93px
  col 2: header "Monthly uptime commitment" · longest unbreakable word 80px · one-line width 182px
  col 3: header "Service credit" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 88px
  col 4: header "Support channels" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 470px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 597px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 596px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare SLA tiers by their uptime commitments, service credits, and support channels.","reading":"Readers scan down the tier names, compare uptime and credit values across tiers, and read across each row to see the support included.","groups":["Monthly uptime commitment and service credit are compact, comparable numeric terms of the SLA.","Support channels is descriptive text associated with each tier and needs the most room for natural wrapping."],"keep_intact":["Tier names, especially Mission-critical","Uptime percentages and service credit percentages","Individual words and support-channel terms"],"may_wrap":["Monthly uptime commitment and Service credit headers","Support channels descriptions at spaces or between listed channels","Header wrapping can use height shared across the header row; support text can use height shared across each data row."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [114, 145, 109, 228] · table 597×214px · row heights [53, 33, 73, 53] · column headers wrapped 1/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [105, 125, 90, 276] · table 597×194px · row heights [53, 33, 53, 53] · column headers wrapped 2/4 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [114, 203, 100, 179] · table 597×254px · row heights [53, 33, 94, 73] · column headers wrapped 1/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
